gen-gf-gabarito-gf-sawarabi-gothic: Gabarito has no hairlines and no swells, just a flat, confident line. Sawarabi Gothic is just as low in contrast, with curves that gape open, so the two share one steady, unfussy line quality.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-shanti: Gabarito's round letters carry walls every bit as weighty as its straight strokes, which gives its headings a distinctive, expressive presence. Shanti then adds a generous entry into the e's eye, quietly modern.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-shippori-antique: Terminals sliced open let the letters breathe outward in Gabarito, a display face that looks drawn in one continuous pen stroke. Shippori Antique's monoweight sans skeleton keeps that openness going.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-shippori-antique-b1: Gabarito looks drawn with one nib, its ends cut open and expressive. Shippori Antique B1 stays modern and plain, daylight showing through every curve, and Gabarito belongs up in display-sized lines.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-sn-pro: Expressive and distinctive, Gabarito draws each letter with a pen line that never changes width. And SN Pro, modern and neutral, keeps open apertures throughout the alphabet, giving that line room to breathe.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-sour-gummy: Distinctive from the first letter, Gabarito looks bent from one length of tubing. Sour Gummy does the quieter job, with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp while the heading handles attitude.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-spinnaker: Expressive rounded strokes, like cut lengths of cord, define Gabarito. That display voice belongs in oversized, brief headings, while modern Spinnaker's apertures keep counters connected to the space outside.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-stick: A one-nib drawn look and openly cut ends give Gabarito a distinctive, expressive character in headings. Stick's tubelike lines stay modern across paragraphs, with exits wide enough to pass light through.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tasa-explorer: Gabarito does the loud work, holding a stencil-cut channel's constant weight across big display letters. TASA Explorer handles the quiet part, its clean sans-serif curves ending like brush strokes lifted early.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-telex: Zero modulation runs through Gabarito, giving its expressive, display-sized letters a distinctive, uniform line. While Gabarito shouts, Telex's curvy, unclamped letters do the quieter work of staying clean and readable.
